title: runner_enforced blindness is Codex-only, so experience metrics are Codex-only
body:
`runner_enforced` — the evidence class that gates every experience metric — can only be
produced by Codex. Every other vendor fails at launch with "Could not resolve the
existing Codex home; pure run refused."

Found by running one real live player through playtest-loop.sh with `claude_code`. It is
not a stray hard-coding: blind-tester/run.sh resolves a Codex home unconditionally for
every provider (`RAW_CODEX_HOME="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}"`) and refuses pure mode
when it is absent, because the proof of blindness is read back out of Codex's own
rollout logs.

The machinery behind that proof is Codex-shaped end to end and has no counterpart:

  blind-tester/codex-rollout.mjs         1,566 lines — resolve-home, validate-output,
                                         resolve/verify-client-binary, preflight-client,
                                         render-client-authority, capture
  blind-tester/codex-process-anchor.mjs
  blind-tester/codex-pure-envelope.mjs
  blind-tester/codex-strict-stream.mjs

Zero equivalents for claude_code, gemini_cli or any future vendor.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY COSTS

Multi-vendor bug corroboration is unaffected: `operator_attested` sessions count toward
it, and cross-family agreement is the promotion rung that matters. What is lost is
multi-vendor EXPERIENCE measurement — retention, clarity and enjoyment take
runner_enforced sessions only, so every headline experience number in this repo is
currently a measurement of Codex specifically, not of players in general. A cheap
mass-parallel Gemini fleet cannot move those numbers no matter how large it is.

That is a real limit on the two-loop design's premise, which is that volume and vendor
diversity are what make the survey worth trusting.

WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT ALREADY

- docs/two_loop_workflow.md claimed "Nothing in this repo privileges a vendor" and gave
  `PLAYTEST_COHORT="gemini_cli:8,codex:2"` as an example, in which all eight Gemini
  players would have failed. Corrected to state the constraint plainly.
- playtest-loop.sh now refuses a non-Codex live cohort up front, naming the ingest path
  instead. Previously every player died on the Codex-home error and the recorder — which
  cannot distinguish a launch refusal from a mid-play crash — filed each as a `failed`
  session, seeding the corpus with fake data points carrying a real vendor family.

WHAT IS LEFT

Per-vendor capture, so a non-Codex CLI can earn runner_enforced. The shape of the work
is one reader per vendor answering what codex-rollout.mjs answers: which binary ran,
under which cwd and argv, and what tools the session actually touched. Claude Code and
Gemini CLI both write session logs; whether those logs carry enough to prove the tool
allowlist is the open question and should be answered before committing to the work.

Worth deciding explicitly rather than drifting: either build per-vendor capture, or
narrow the documented promise to "any model can play; one vendor can be PROVEN blind"
and stop treating experience metrics as fleet-wide.

evidence.summary: A live claude_code player failed at launch; the pure-run proof is built on Codex rollout logs with no equivalent for any other vendor.
